verdict.rationale: TruffleHog ships well-documented pre-commit and pre-receive git hooks (trufflehog-docs-5, -13, -19, -20, -26, -30, -31) that scan code for secrets before it is committed, which can technically catch AI-generated code paths through standard git hooks or CI. However there is no evidence of any specific integration point for coding agents (e.g., an MCP server, IDE/agent plugin, or agent-specific pre-generation hook) — it's a generic pre-commit mechanism, not an AI-agent-aware wiring. Missing for 10: explicit coding-agent/AI-tool integration (MCP server, agent plugin, or IDE hook), evidence of scanning AI-generated code specifically, and independent confirmation the pre-commit flow works well with agent-driven commit workflows.
